# On the Existence of $\tilde{G}_2$-Structures on 7-Manifolds

The paper addresses a fundamental question in the geometry of exceptional structures: under what conditions does a 7-dimensional manifold admit a $\tilde{G}_2$-structure? The central contribution of this work is the establishment of a necessary and sufficient condition characterizing precisely when a compact 7-manifold carries such a structure. This result is significant because it provides a complete answer—rather than a partial or merely sufficient criterion—for the compact setting, effectively settling the existence question in this case.

The characterization obtained is both topological and geometric in nature, drawing on the algebraic properties of the structure group $\tilde{G}_2$ and its action on the tangent bundle, together with the obstruction theory germane to reductions of the structure group of the frame bundle. Because the criterion is if-and-only-if, it furnishes a definitive tool: given any compact 7-manifold, one can in principle verify whether the topological invariants in question are satisfied, and thereby conclude the existence (or nonexistence) of a $\tilde{G}_2$-structure without further geometric analysis. This stands in contrast to many existence problems in geometric structure theory, where only sufficient conditions are typically available, and underscores the completeness of the result restricted to the compact category.

Building upon this foundational theorem, the authors extend their investigation to the noncompact setting by considering open 7-manifolds. Here, the primary goal shifts from characterizing $\tilde{G}_2$-structures per se to establishing conditions guaranteeing the existence of a *closed* 3-form of $\tilde{G}_2$-type—a stronger geometric object that, when it exists, endows the manifold with additional integrability properties beyond the mere reduction of structure group. The authors succeed in deriving a sufficient condition for this existence problem in the open case, obtained as a consequence of, and building directly upon, the compact classification result.

It is important to note that the transition from the compact to the open case necessarily involves a weakening of the type of statement obtained: while the compact result yields a full equivalence, the open manifold result furnishes only a sufficient condition. This asymmetry is not a shortcoming of the analysis but rather reflects an intrinsic feature of noncompact geometry, where the lack of compactness introduces significant additional complexity—issues such as the behavior of forms and structures at infinity, the failure of standard obstruction-theoretic arguments to directly generalize, and the need for auxiliary hypotheses (such as controlled ends or exhaustion techniques) that are unnecessary in the compact case. Consequently, achieving a matching necessary condition for the open case remains a more delicate problem, left open by the current work.

Taken together, these results forge an important connection between the mere existence of a $\tilde{G}_2$-structure (understood as a reduction of the structure group) and the stronger differential-geometric requirement of a closed 3-form realizing this structure. This linkage highlights a recurring theme in the study of special geometric structures: the passage from an algebraic or topological reduction of the structure group to an honest closed (or otherwise integrable) differential form representing that structure is often a substantial additional step, requiring techniques beyond pure obstruction theory. By carefully establishing the compact case completely and then leveraging it to obtain sufficient conditions in the open case, the paper provides a coherent and comprehensive framework for understanding $\tilde{G}_2$-structures across both compact and noncompact 7-manifolds.

# Topological Conditions for $\tilde{G}_2$-Structures on 7-Manifolds

## Introduction

The study of exceptional holonomy geometries has become a central theme in differential geometry, particularly since Berger's classification of possible holonomy groups of Riemannian manifolds. Among these exceptional cases, $G_2$-structures on 7-manifolds have attracted significant attention due to their rich geometric and topological properties, as well as their connections to string theory and M-theory in theoretical physics. A closely related but distinct structure is the $\tilde{G}_2$-structure, associated with the non-compact real form of the exceptional Lie group $G_2$, which arises naturally in the study of pseudo-Riemannian metrics of signature $(3,4)$ on 7-manifolds.

This paper addresses a fundamental question in this area: under what topological conditions can a 7-manifold admit a $\tilde{G}_2$-structure? While the existence of $G_2$-structures on compact 7-manifolds has been well-studied and characterized in terms of the vanishing of certain characteristic classes, the analogous problem for $\tilde{G}_2$-structures—corresponding to the split or non-compact real form—presents additional subtleties due to the indefinite signature of the associated bilinear form.

## Main Results and Methodology

The central contribution of this work is the establishment of a necessary and sufficient topological condition for a compact 7-manifold to admit a $\tilde{G}_2$-structure. This is achieved through a careful analysis of the obstruction theory associated with the reduction of the structure group of the tangent bundle from $GL(7,\mathbb{R})$ to $\tilde{G}_2 \subset SO(3,4)$.

Our approach builds upon and extends classical techniques used in the study of $G$-structures, incorporating tools from algebraic topology such as characteristic class computations, obstruction theory, and the analysis of homotopy groups of relevant classifying spaces. Specifically, we analyze the topological obstructions arising from the inclusion $\tilde{G}_2 \hookrightarrow SO(3,4)$ and relate these to more familiar and computable topological invariants of the manifold, such as the Stiefel-Whitney classes, the Euler characteristic, and spin-related invariants.

The key theorem establishes that a compact, orientable 7-manifold $M$ admits a $\tilde{G}_2$-structure if and only if a specific combination of characteristic classes vanishes, subject to additional conditions related to the existence of a compatible metric of signature $(3,4)$. This criterion is both computationally tractable and geometrically illuminating, as it connects the existence of the exotic $\tilde{G}_2$-structure to more classical topological data.

## Extension to Open Manifolds

Building upon this compact case result, we extend our analysis to the setting of open (non-compact) 7-manifolds. While the compact case naturally admits a full necessary and sufficient characterization due to the finiteness of relevant cohomological data, the open case requires additional care due to the lack of compactness and the potential for non-trivial behavior at infinity.

In this setting, we focus on establishing a sufficient condition for an open 7-manifold to admit not merely a $\tilde{G}_2$-structure, but one satisfying the stronger geometric condition of being *closed* as a differential 3-form. This closedness condition is particularly significant, as it is closely related to the existence of torsion-free $\tilde{G}_2$-structures, which in turn correspond to pseudo-Riemannian metrics with special holonomy contained in $\tilde{G}_2$.

Our method for the open case leverages the compact result via an exhaustion argument, combined with careful control of the topological obstructions on each compact piece of an exhaustion of the open manifold. We show that under certain conditions on the topology at infinity—formulated precisely in terms of the vanishing of obstruction classes on a cofinal system of compact submanifolds with boundary—one can construct a global closed 3-form of $\tilde{G}_2$-type on the entire open manifold.

## Significance and Applications

The results presented in this paper contribute to the broader classification program of manifolds admitting geometric structures related to exceptional holonomy groups. By establishing precise topological criteria for the existence of $\tilde{G}_2$-structures, we provide concrete tools for identifying new examples of manifolds with these structures, as well as necessary conditions that can rule out their existence on certain manifolds.

Furthermore, the connection to closed 3-forms of $\tilde{G}_2$-type is particularly relevant for the construction of manifolds with holonomy contained in the split real form $\tilde{G}_2$, which are of interest both from a purely geometric standpoint and due to their appearance in certain physical theories involving pseudo-Riemannian geometries of split signature.

We conclude with a discussion of potential applications of these results, including the construction of explicit examples of open 7-manifolds admitting closed $\tilde{G}_2$-structures, as well as directions for future research, such as extending these topological criteria to address the existence of torsion-free structures and exploring the moduli space of such geometries on both compact and non-compact 7-manifolds.

# The Language of Discovery: "We Find a..."

In the world of scientific writing, few phrases carry as much weight as "We find a." These three words, unassuming as they may seem, often signal the moment when abstract hypotheses meet concrete evidence—the pivotal juncture where research transforms into knowledge.

## A Phrase Rooted in Empiricism

The phrase appears constantly across disciplines: physics, biology, economics, computer science, and beyond. "We find a significant correlation between..." "We find a novel mechanism that..." "We find a surprising pattern in the data..." Each instance represents a claim—modest in tone, yet profound in implication. The word "find" suggests discovery rather than invention, implying that the pattern or relationship being described already existed in nature, waiting to be uncovered.

## The Humility and Confidence Embedded in Language

What makes this phrase interesting linguistically is its balance of humility and authority. Unlike stronger declarations such as "We prove" or "We demonstrate conclusively," saying "we find" acknowledges the provisional nature of scientific knowledge. It suggests observation rather than absolute truth, leaving room for future researchers to build upon, refine, or even overturn the finding. Yet at the same time, the phrase carries genuine confidence—it is not "we suspect" or "we speculate," but a statement grounded in evidence and methodology.

## Why This Matters

Understanding how researchers communicate their findings offers insight into the broader culture of science itself. The careful phrasing used in academic papers reflects deep-seated norms: transparency about uncertainty, respect for peer review, and an ongoing commitment to revising our understanding of the world as new evidence emerges. The next time you encounter the phrase "we find a" in a research paper, consider it not just as a stylistic convention, but as a small window into the scientific process—one grounded in curiosity, rigor, and the collective pursuit of truth.

# Abstract

We investigate existence conditions for G₂-structures on smooth 7-manifolds, addressing both the compact and open (non-compact) settings within a unified topological and analytic framework. A G₂-structure on a 7-manifold $M$ is defined by a stable 3-form $\varphi$ inducing a Riemannian metric $g_\varphi$ and orientation, whose existence is governed by an underlying reduction of the frame bundle structure group to $G_2 \subset SO(7)$.

In the compact case, we establish that the existence of a G₂-structure is equivalent to a purely topological condition: $M$ must be orientable and spin, with the additional requirement that the associated obstruction class in $H^3(M;\mathbb{Z})$ (or equivalently, a suitable characteristic class condition tied to the triviality of the tangent bundle up to rank considerations) vanishes. We show this is equivalent to the existence of a reduction of the structure group of $TM$ to $G_2$, which by classical obstruction theory reduces to the vanishing of the first two Stiefel-Whitney classes and a mod-2 reduction of a further obstruction in dimension 7, since $G_2$ is 2-connected and the relevant homotopy groups $\pi_i(SO(7)/G_2)$ vanish appropriately through the relevant range. We further analyze refinements distinguishing the existence of general (non-integrable) G₂-structures from those admitting torsion-free, closed, or coclosed refinements, linking these to curvature and holonomy constraints.

For open manifolds, we invoke the Gromov-Eliashberg h-principle machinery, showing that existence of formal G₂-structures — bundle-theoretic solutions to the relevant differential relation — implies existence of genuine (in particular, closed) G₂-structures via convex integration techniques, with no further topological obstruction beyond orientability, spin condition, and the formal solvability of the underlying linear algebra problem. This yields a sharp dichotomy: on open manifolds, topological necessary conditions are also sufficient, while on compact manifolds additional global constraints — including a version of an index-type obstruction connecting the Euler class and Pontryagin classes with the existence of closed G₂-structures — must be verified, and are related to (but distinct from) the stronger existence question for torsion-free structures with holonomy contained in $G_2$.

Our results synthesize prior work of Gray, Friedrich–Kath–Moroianu–Semmelmann, and Crowley–Nordström on topological classification with h-principle techniques for open manifolds, providing a comprehensive existence criterion applicable across both regimes, and clarifying the precise gap between formal and genuine solutions in the compact setting that must be closed by PDE methods (e.g., Joyce's gluing constructions) rather than soft topological techniques.

# Abstract

We investigate the existence of split (or "para") G₂-structures on 7-manifolds, corresponding to the noncompact real form of G₂ preserving a stable 3-form of split signature. We establish that a compact 7-manifold M admits a split G₂-structure if and only if it admits a stable 3-form ω whose associated bilinear form has signature (3,4), together with a compatible reduction of the structure group of TM to the split form G₂*. Equivalently, in terms of characteristic classes, we show that such a structure exists precisely when M is orientable, admits a rank-3 distribution (or equivalently a reduction to SL(3,ℝ) × SL(4,ℝ)/ℤ₂-type structure), and satisfies appropriate compatibility conditions on the Euler and Stiefel–Whitney classes ensuring the existence of the required stable form up to homotopy. This parallels the h-principle techniques used in the Riemannian G₂ case, but requires care due to the indefinite nature of the associated metric.

For open (noncompact) manifolds, we prove a full existence result: every open 7-manifold M admitting an almost split G₂-structure in the formal/topological sense (i.e., a topological reduction of the frame bundle to G₂*) also admits a genuine split G₂-structure, homotopic to the given one. This follows from Gromov's h-principle for open manifolds, exploiting the flexibility of the split condition, in contrast to the more rigid torsion-free case. As a consequence, the existence problem for split G₂-structures on open manifolds reduces entirely to algebraic topology.

# Abstract

We investigate the topological constraints imposed on 7-manifolds admitting closed 3-forms whose pointwise stabilizer is the exceptional Lie group G₂, distinguishing structures according to the co-closedness of the associated 4-form and the compactness of the underlying manifold. On compact 7-manifolds, we show that torsion-free G₂-structures—arising as solutions to the full system dφ = 0, d⋆φ = 0—force strong restrictions on the fundamental group, the first Betti number, and the ring structure of real cohomology, consistent with the holonomy reduction Hol ⊆ G₂ and the associated Ricci-flatness. In particular, we analyze how the decomposition of Λ²T*M and Λ³T*M into G₂-irreducible summands interacts with Hodge theory to bound harmonic representatives and constrain the possible values of b₂ and b₃, drawing on known examples obtained via Joyce-type resolutions of orbifolds and twisted connected sums. By contrast, in the non-compact setting we demonstrate that the closedness condition dφ = 0 alone, without properness or completeness assumptions on the metric, permits substantially richer topology: we construct families of non-compact 7-manifolds with unbounded Betti numbers and non-finitely generated cohomology admitting closed (but not co-closed) G₂ structures, showing the torsion-free condition's topological rigidity is intimately tied to compactness via Hodge-theoretic arguments and the maximum principle applied to the associated harmonic forms. We further discuss the role of asymptotically conical and asymptotically cylindrical geometries as intermediate regimes, where partial topological control is recovered through prescribed asymptotic cohomology data, linking our results to the classification programs for complete Ricci-flat G₂ metrics. Our findings clarify the extent to which the interplay between exceptional holonomy and global topology is a fundamentally compact phenomenon, with non-compact analogues governed instead by asymptotic and boundary conditions rather than closed-manifold cohomological identities.

# Theorem: Characterization of Compact 7-Manifolds Admitting a $\tilde{G}_2$-Structure

**Abstract Summary**

This theorem addresses the existence problem for **$\tilde{G}_2$-structures** on compact 7-manifolds, where $\tilde{G}_2$ denotes the split (non-compact) real form of the exceptional Lie group $G_2$, as opposed to the compact form associated with classical $G_2$-structures. A $\tilde{G}_2$-structure corresponds to a stable 3-form of "split type," inducing a metric of **signature $(3,4)$** rather than the Riemannian metric arising from ordinary $G_2$-structures.

**Main Result:** A compact 7-manifold $M$ admits a $\tilde{G}_2$-structure if and only if it admits an **almost bi-Lagrangian structure** — equivalently, a splitting of the tangent bundle
$$
TM \cong E \oplus F
$$
into complementary distributions of ranks 3 and 4 (or an appropriate rank pairing determined by the split form), together with compatible topological reductions of the structure group. This is equivalent to the existence of a reduction of the frame bundle's structure group from $GL(7,\mathbb{R})$ to $\tilde{G}_2 \subset SO(3,4)$, characterized cohomologically by the vanishing of specific obstruction classes (analogous to spin-type conditions), rather than by curvature or definiteness conditions as in the Riemannian $G_2$ case.

Equivalently, the existence is governed by purely **topological data**: the manifold must admit a rank-3 (or rank-4) sub-bundle of the tangent bundle satisfying compatibility conditions with an orientation and a chosen volume form, reducing the problem to standard obstruction theory for bundle reductions.

**Application to Open Manifolds and Closed 3-Forms**

As a consequence, the theorem yields an **h-principle type result** for open 7-manifolds: every closed 3-form of split type representing a formal solution (i.e., satisfying the algebraic stability/split condition pointwise) can be deformed, through the Gromov–Phillips convex integration technique, to an actual **closed $\tilde{G}_2$-structure** (i.e., $d\varphi = 0$) whenever the underlying almost bi-Lagrangian topological reduction exists. This provides:

- A method to construct **torsion-free or closed split $G_2$-structures** on open manifolds without curvature obstructions, in contrast to the compact Riemannian $G_2$ setting where Ricci-flatness imposes strong global constraints.
- A demonstration that, unlike the Riemannian case, the existence of closed $\tilde{G}_2$-structures on *open* manifolds is governed purely by **soft, topological (h-principle) methods**, since the indefinite signature removes the ellipticity obstructions present in the definite $G_2$ setting.

# Abstract

We establish a topological criterion for the existence of a split-signature $G_2^*$-structure on a compact, orientable 7-manifold $M$. Since $G_2^* = G_{2(2)}$ acts transitively on $\mathbb{R}^7$ with isotropy $SL(3,\mathbb{R})$, a reduction of the frame bundle of $M$ to $G_2^*$ is equivalent to the existence of a 3-plane distribution or, equivalently, a rank-3 stable subbundle of $TM$ together with a compatible splitting $TM \cong E^3 \oplus F^4$ inducing the required conformal split metric of signature $(3,4)$. We show that such a reduction exists if and only if $M$ admits a rank-3 subbundle $E \subset TM$ satisfying
$$
w_1(E) = w_1(TM), \qquad w_2(TM) = w_2(E) + w_2(TM/E) + w_1(E)\,w_1(TM/E),
$$
together with the vanishing of a secondary obstruction class $\theta(E) \in H^3(M; \mathbb{Z}/2)$ arising from the difference of spin structures induced on $E$ and $TM/E$ once the primary Stiefel–Whitney obstructions vanish. Equivalently, in terms of the classifying map $\tau: M \to BO(7)$, a $G_2^*$-structure exists iff $\tau$ lifts through the fibration $B\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R}) \to BO(3)\times BO(4) \to BO(7)$ classified by the above characteristic classes, together with the mod-2 obstruction $\theta$. In particular, since $G_2^*$ is homotopy equivalent to $SL(3,\mathbb{R}) \times SO(3)$'s common maximal compact $SO(3)\times SO(3)/\mathbb{Z}_2$... [continued reduction to $SO(3)$-bundle obstruction theory], the existence problem reduces entirely to the vanishing of $w_1(M)$-twisted Stiefel–Whitney classes of an auxiliary rank-3 bundle, paralleling the classical Gray–Friedrich criterion $w_1(M) = w_2(M) = 0$ for the compact Riemannian $G_2$ case.

**Corollary (noncompact case).** If $M$ is a noncompact 7-manifold with the homotopy type of a CW complex of dimension $\le 6$ (e.g. an open manifold admitting a handle decomposition without top handles, or more generally satisfying $H^7(M;\mathbb{Z}/2\text{-twisted})=0$), then all obstructions above vanish automatically, and $M$ admits a split $G_2^*$-structure if and only if it is parallelizable in the stable sense $w_1(M) = w_2(M) = 0$; in particular every open (noncompact, no closed component) orientable spin 7-manifold admits a split-signature $G_2$ structure.
